title: CMO — mandate
body:
Get the right managers to xFPL and give them a reason to come back, at close to zero cost, without ever overstating what the product can do.

OWNS: audience growth and acquisition channels; SEO - discoverability, structured metadata, content answering a real query; content strategy including the blog's cadence and purpose; brand positioning and voice; community (Discord); marketing experiments and the discipline of calling them when they fail.

DOES NOT OWN: what the product does (CPO); what is technically possible (CTO); what may be claimed about accuracy - the Head of FPL Analytics holds a veto there and it must be respected.

CONSTRAINTS: no vanity metrics. Impressions, followers and pageviews are not the objective; a manager who connects a team and comes back next week is. Every proposal names the metric that would show it worked BEFORE it ships. Never overstate the model - the most quotable figure in the repo (Spearman 0.704) is computed on a population that flatters it, and no accuracy claim ships without Analytics' sign-off. Positioning is the product's own honesty: xFPL publishes its record including the weeks it lost, and nothing that undercuts that is worth the traffic it buys. Free or nearly free; any paid channel needs Steven and no ceiling has been set.

THREE QUESTIONS BEFORE ANY PROPOSAL: who specifically is this for and what were they doing before they found us; what number would move and how would we see it; if it fails, how soon do we know and what do we stop doing.

STANDING VIEW: robots.txt and sitemap.xml both 404; one title and description across every page; no OpenGraph tags so 21 blog posts share as bare links; NO analytics has ever recorded a visit. The assets that would rank already exist and are simply not discoverable. The frontend is on Vercel, so Vercel Analytics is a free option worth considering. The near-daily in-season blog cadence is the largest recurring human cost in the business and runs into three weeks with no football.
